 Warriors make major decision on Bucks center in Kristaps Porzingis trade 
 2026-11-10 00:51 
 The Bucks are open to trading Myles Turner, but the Warriors remain unwilling to include additional draft assets to make a potential deal for Kristaps Porzingis happen.
 Credit: AP - Scanpix 
 Credit AP - Scanpix 
 Credit AP - Scanpix

 The Golden State Warriors have reportedly maintained their firm stance on Kristaps Porzingis' trade situation with the Milwaukee Bucks.

 According to Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints, the Warriors remain unwilling to attach draft assets amid the Bucks' openness to obtain Kristaps Porzingis' contract in exchange for Myles Turner.
 "While willing to give up Myles Turner for Porzingis’ contract, the Bucks have wanted draft compensation from the Warriors, something that isn’t on the table," the report indicated.
 "Golden State has held firm that if it were to absorb Turner’s contract for Porzingis and another player, presumably Moses Moody, the team would need extra compensation from Milwaukee."
 Warriors continue to work for Kristaps Porzingis trade
 The Golden State Warriors continue to signal within the NBA market that Kristaps Porzingis is available for a trade.
 The Latvian star notably penned a personal statement announcing that he is stepping away from the game to focus on his health. Accordingly, Porzingis also made it clear that he will work toward a resolution with the Warriors regarding his future.
 Porzingis, who inked a two-year, $40 million contract with the Dubs this past offseason, has been nonexistent for the Warriors since Media Day. The NBA star has been dealing with POTS (Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome), with past reports suggesting that he is contemplating retirement.
 Warriors make firm stance amid Myles Turner struggles
 As first reported by NBA insiders Marc Stein and Jake Fischer, the Golden State Warriors are uninterested in attaching draft capital just to move Kristaps Porzingis' salary. However, the Dubs will entertain the possibility for a right player available.
 So far, Myles Turner has been disappointing to start this 2026-27 NBA season. The Milwaukee Bucks big man is averaging just 7.1 points and 5.7 rebounds while shooting 34.6% from the field across 10 games.
 Turner is currently playing under a hefty four-year, $108.9 million fully guaranteed contract that he signed with the Bucks in last year's offseason.
 With Turner struggling, the Dubs will continue to be convinced about their demands in any potential deals around Porzingis.
